title.en: Explain why Ampere's circuital law needed correction

body.en: Apply *Ampere's* law to a loop around the wire of a charging capacitor. A flat surface through the loop is cut by the current $i$, but a pot-shaped surface passing between the plates is cut by no current at all. The same loop gives two different answers, so the law as written is incomplete.
body.kn: ಆವೇಶಗೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತಿರುವ ಧಾರಕದ ತಂತಿಯ ಸುತ್ತ ಆಂಪಿಯರ್ ನಿಯಮ ಅನ್ವಯಿಸಿದರೆ, ಸಮತಟ್ಟಾದ ಮೇಲ್ಮೈಗೆ ಪ್ರವಾಹ i ಸಿಗುತ್ತದೆ, ಆದರೆ ಫಲಕಗಳ ನಡುವೆ ಹಾದುಹೋಗುವ ಮೇಲ್ಮೈಗೆ ಶೂನ್ಯ. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ನಿಯಮ ಅಪೂರ್ಣ.

say.en: When a capacitor charges, current flows in the wires but no charge crosses the gap between the plates.
Ampere's law around the wire gives a magnetic field, but a surface passing through the gap encloses zero current. The law contradicts itself.
Between the plates the electric field grows as charge builds up. Maxwell said this changing electric flux acts like a current.
Adding this displacement current gives the Ampere–Maxwell law. The total current is continuous through the gap.

narration.en: While the capacitor charges, a conduction current i flows in the wires but no charge crosses the gap. There the electric field is changing, and Maxwell's displacement current i_d = ε0 dΦE/dt equals i. That is why the magnetic field (circles) is the same around the wire and around the gap.

body.en: Between the plates the electric flux $\Phi_E = q/\varepsilon_0$ grows as the charge grows. Maxwell called $\varepsilon_0\, d\Phi_E/dt$ the *displacement current*. It equals the conduction current in the wires, so current is continuous all round the circuit. A changing electric field produces a magnetic field, just as a changing magnetic field produces an electric field.
body.kn: ಫಲಕಗಳ ನಡುವೆ ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಅಭಿವಾಹ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಮ್ಯಾಕ್ಸ್‌ವೆಲ್ ε₀ dΦ_E/dt ಅನ್ನು ಸ್ಥಾನಪಲ್ಲಟ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಎಂದು ಕರೆದರು. ಇದು ತಂತಿಯ ವಾಹಕ ಪ್ರವಾಹಕ್ಕೆ ಸಮ. ಬದಲಾಗುವ ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರವು ಕಾಂತಕ್ಷೇತ್ರವನ್ನು ಉಂಟುಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: The plates of a capacitor have area 0.01 m². The electric field between them changes at 1.13 × 10¹² V m⁻¹ s⁻¹. Find the displacement current.

steps.en: i_d = ε₀ dΦ_E/dt = ε₀ A dE/dt.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. The plates of a capacitor have area 0.01 m². The electric field between them changes at 1.13 × 10¹² V m⁻¹ s⁻¹. Find the displacement current.

say.en: Let us solve this together. The plates of a capacitor have area 0.01 square metres. The electric field between them changes at 1.13 times 10 to the power 12 volts m to the power minus 1 s to the power minus 1. Find the displacement current.
i d equals epsilon 0 dΦ_E/dt equals epsilon 0 A dE over dt.
i d equals 8.85 times 10 to the power minus 12 times 0.01 times 1.13 times 10 to the power 12.
i d is approximately 0.10 A.
So the answer is 0.1 A.

problem.en: A 2 μF capacitor is connected to a source whose voltage rises at 5000 V/s. Find the displacement current between the plates.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A 2 μF capacitor is connected to a source whose voltage rises at 5000 V/s. Find the displacement current between the plates.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A 2 microfarads capacitor is connected to a source whose voltage rises at 5000 volts per second. Find the displacement current between the plates.
i d equals C dV over dt.
i d equals 2 times 10 to the power minus 6 times 5 times 10 to the power 3 equals 1 times 10 to the power minus 2 A.
So the answer is 10 milliamperes.

body.en: In any charging or discharging capacitor problem, the displacement current between the plates is exactly the conduction current in the wires. Do not compute flux unless asked for the field inside.
